_notes: The friar's discretionary week. E3 §3.3 'Discretionary spends': what a friar gives his free blocks to, on top of the horarium, the office, and the work. Rates are per block per week; a reputation at three blocks a week is known in about two years and well known in four. Reputations accrue only as far as the stat gates allow (systems/religious/reputations.ts). Sunday supply pays the house; observance moves the friar's own observance against the house's. Tunables invented.

spends.label: Study
spends.blurb: The library, the desk, the argument with a dead man. The largest single category for a religious.
digest: The desk had you for the evenings.
The library, and the argument with Thomas.
Hours at the desk, and the house noticed the light.
A commentary open on the desk past Compline, and the pencil notes in the margin.
Greek, an hour a day, the verbs no kinder than they were in the studium.
The journal articles you had been saving, read at last, two of them twice.

spends.label: Degree and research work
spends.blurb: A multi-year background commitment: a thesis, an edition, a book. Far more common here than in a diocese.
digest: The chapter is a page longer.
The research went on; the footnotes are the year.
An afternoon in the archive that did not end.

spends.label: Teaching
spends.blurb: A house of studies, a school, a university. For many friars the primary work, not a side path.
digest: Four sections, and one of them woke up.
The lecture, and the questions after it that were the lecture.
Grading, which is teaching by other means.

spends.label: Confessions
spends.blurb: The box, week after week. Friars are the Church's confessors, and this is central here in a way it never is for a busy pastor.
digest: The Saturday line, and the Tuesday one that has begun.
Confessions until the church was dark.
The box, and the man who came back.
An hour in the box before the noon Mass, and a woman who had waited thirty years.
The box on Saturday afternoon, and a boy who confessed he had come because his mother made him, and then stayed.
Confessions after the evening Mass, and the absolution said more times than you counted.

spends.label: Preaching missions and retreats
spends.blurb: Travel, days at a time, four nights in a parish that did not want one.
digest: Four nights in a parish two dioceses over.
A retreat weekend, and the drive back in the dark.
The mission, and the pastor's confessional line after it.

spends.label: Sunday supply
spends.blurb: Covering Masses at diocesan parishes. Unglamorous, recurring, and valuable: money for the house, your name across a whole diocese, and your Sundays gone.
digest: Two Masses in a parish forty miles off, and the pastor's thanks.
Sunday supply: the envelope for the house, the drive, the people who asked your name.
A parish the diocese cannot staff had a friar this Sunday.

spends.label: Monastic observance
spends.blurb: Silence, lectio, adoration, the night office, manual labour, chant, fasting. Builds piety and the reputation for holiness, and advances nothing worldly whatsoever.
digest: The night office, alone, and the silence after it.
Lectio, and the hour of adoration nobody scheduled.
The garden, the fast, the chant practised twice.
The rosary walked in the cloister after supper, the beads worn smooth by other men.
An hour before the Blessed Sacrament at dawn, the house asleep.
The Office said slowly, in choir, the psalms given their full weight.

spends.label: The liturgy
spends.blurb: Invested liturgy, the chant, the ceremonies, and training others in them. Beautiful worship draws people, and divides them.
digest: The schola, and the Sunday that was sung.
Vespers rehearsed until it was Vespers.
The ceremonies taught to men who had not been taught them.

spends.label: Spiritual direction of others
spends.blurb: Hours with men who have asked, sealed. You form the formators.
digest: Three hours in the parlour with the door closed.
Direction, which is mostly listening.
A man who said the thing, and the hour it took.

spends.label: Writing and publishing
spends.blurb: Articles, a column, a book. The province reads it, and so, sometimes, does the world.
digest: Six hundred words that took the week.
A chapter drafted and thrown away.
The column went in; the letters came back.

spends.label: Community building
spends.blurb: The old friar who needs company, the young one who needs a listener, the table kept late. What the house is for.
digest: The table ran late on purpose.
An evening with the old friar, who talked.
The house was a little more one this week.
Recreation, and a card game the old men have been playing since the council.
A walk after supper with a brother you had not spoken to in a month.
The dishes on Sunday night, four friars and one towel, and a long argument about nothing.

spends.label: Works of mercy
spends.blurb: The shelter, the kitchen, the prison, the immigrant office. The poor, and public witness for them.
digest: The kitchen on Tuesday, and the line down the block.
The jail, and the man who wanted to talk.
A letter to the paper about the shelter, signed.
The soup kitchen on Saturday, and a man who asked for a blessing with his tray.
A day at the immigration office with a family who had no English and a letter they could not read.
The shelter at night, cots and coffee, and the conversation that starts at two in the morning.

spends.label: Campus and street work
spends.blurb: The unchurched and the curious: the campus, the RCIA, the street, the door. Vocations follow evangelists.
digest: Thursday night on the campus, which ran late.
Two inquirers who came back, and one who did not.
The door, and the man who had a question.

spends.label: The hospital and the dying
spends.blurb: Hospitals, hospice, deathbeds, grief. The least glamorous work and the one laypeople never forget.
digest: Two in the morning, the intensive care unit, and a family told.
The hospice, where nobody is in a hurry.
A deathbed, and the prayers said right.

spends.label: Buildings, budgets, and broken things
spends.blurb: The roof, the books, the failing work turned around. You get sent where things are broken.
digest: The roof, the contractor, and the number that was wrong.
A budget balanced by Thursday.
The boiler, which is the parish.

spends.label: Benefactors and the civic table
spends.blurb: Donors, the chancery, the county foundation, the men who fund a roof. Money and access, faintly suspect among the brothers.
digest: Dinner with a man whose name is on a wing.
The foundation board, and the mayor's speech.
A cheque for the house, and a lunch that cost it.

spends.label: The rite of the order
spends.blurb: A Mass in the order's own rite, by leave, at a side altar or for the lay Dominicans' feasts. Rare, and remembered by the men who care either way.
digest: The rite, at the side altar, with one server and whoever came.
The chalice at the start, the short Confiteor, the arms. Nine in the chapel.
The lay Dominicans asked for the rite again, and had it.
